body.statement: For \(K=3\) and \(s=(1,1,4)\), the static selector is \[w_1=w_2=\frac{\sqrt2-1}{2},\qquad w_3=2-\sqrt2.\] The active coefficient is \(C=C_3=(6+2\sqrt2)/7\), \(\eta=(2\sqrt2-1)/7\), \(\rho^\star=2\sqrt2-2\), and \(G=(8\sqrt2-4)/7\). The best-arm-elimination witness with \(h=3\) has exponent \(G I_w\), and the terminal witness eliminating arm \(1\) with survivors \(2,3\) also has exponent \(G I_w\).
body.justification: Exact radicals make the early numerical stress test reproducible and destructive if the branch coupling is wrong.
body.gap: No cited source analyzes this heteroskedastic three-arm design; the proposition verifies the most delicate variance profile used to audit the general formula.
body.consumer: Implementers obtain a fixed regression test with \(G\approx1.044815499855\) for quadratic-program and rounding code.
